_design_note: M4 kill-density ablation, upper dose: three peaceful_agent, measured at 4.6x the kill density of three rule_based. It is the extreme rather than the recommendation: it also removes the coin competition entirely (their coins 5.65 -> 0.07) and every bomb but ours, so a win here is not attributable and a loss tells us where the dose stops helping. Run because a dose-response with two points cannot show a turning point.

_predeclared_design_numbers.control: The D1 arm (the same direction at a lower dose) and runs/m4_oppbc_20260901.
_predeclared_design_numbers.evaluation: Judged on the opponent proxy pool (scripts/tournament_pool.py), both board sets, single seeds and the five-seed ensemble. NOTE THE CONTAMINATED CELL: the pool's mixed_weak table contains a peaceful_agent, so for an arm trained on peacefuls that cell is partly familiar and must be reported separately; the verdict rests on coin3, noisyrb3, rb3 and mixed_neural.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: If the pool mean is not above this arm's own baseline, kill-signal density is not a lever on this line and the direction closes.
_predeclared_design_numbers.measured_kill_density: Measured before the arms were written (docs/05 section 0.41), with the epsilon-0 weights over 40 rounds: three rule_based give 0.200 kills a round; swapping ONE for a peaceful changes nothing (0.200); two peacefuls give 0.625 (3.1x) and three give 0.925 (4.6x). Two evaders give 0.075 -- LOWER than three rule_based -- because an agent that never bombs never walks into its own blast, which is what actually kills rule_based (its own suicides are 1.27 a round against peaceful's and evader's 0.00).
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: Highest kills of the three, and the largest risk of a policy that does not transfer: an agent that has never competed for a coin or dodged another agent's bomb for 10000 rounds.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: All five training seeds, kills and suicides beside every score, the tournament curve at every evaluated checkpoint, and the pool as the selection number.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reproducibility: rule_based_agent and peaceful_agent both call np.random.seed() with no argument, and evader_agent does the same, so no arm with opponents is bit-reproducible in training or in evaluation.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_confound_and_its_control: Substituting a peaceful for a rule_based moves three things at once: kill density up, coin competition down (their coins 5.65 -> 3.90) and bomb density down. The evader arm is the control that separates them: it matches the competition and the bomb density of the peaceful table while leaving kill density 8x lower, so the D1-minus-C1 difference is kill density with the rest held roughly fixed. It is NOT a second dose.
_predeclared_design_numbers.why_frequency_and_not_magnitude: The kill signal is the sparsest thing this project trains on: KILLED_OPPONENT is 1.7% of the positive reward and 191 times rarer than a coin (docs/01 section 7.27.2), every epsilon-greedy arm's kill curve peaks near round 3000 and then falls (section 7.41.1), and raising the *value* of a kill was measured as a null -- A07's shaping doubled the bombing rate and moved kills by 0.0002 (section 7.29.3). Raising the *frequency* of kills has never been tried, and the mixed-table arm (section 0.38) is the evidence that it matters: putting two nearly unkillable neural opponents on the training table took kills from 0.520 to 0.106. This is that experiment run in the other direction.
